issues: Column headers 'Rating / Review / Reviewer / Sentiment / Topic / Version / Date' are only visible on md+ (col-span-* grid); mobile view collapses to no headers — acceptable but a small 'view on desktop' hint would improve UX. Non-blocking.

critical_code_review_comments: routes_reviews._date_range mixes ISO date formats — date_from uses 'YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00' (naive) while date_to uses 'YYYY-MM-DDT23:59:59.999999+00:00' (tz-aware). Because reviews.created_at is stored as ISO strings from now_iso() (tz-aware), the string comparison still works but is fragile: if any review is inserted with a naive isoformat, the $gte comparison could misorder. Recommend normalizing both bounds to the same format (either both naive or both with +00:00 offset).

routes_reviews.export_reviews caps results at 20000 rows with .to_list(20000) but neither warns nor paginates — a super_admin export across all orgs could silently truncate. Consider (a) surfacing a warning header if len(rows)==20000, or (b) streaming the CSV via StreamingResponse.

routes_reviews.reviews_summary loads full rating+sentiment lists into memory (.to_list(20000)) and computes counts in Python. For high-volume tenants this should use an aggregation pipeline ($group by rating and $group by sentiment) for perf. Fine at current seed scale.

LiveReviews.jsx filters live-apps as (a.source === 'google_play_live' || a.google_play_status === 'connected'). Since seeded demo apps carry google_play_status='not_connected', this correctly hides demo. Confirmed via UI (only 'Aarohi' — a previously-synced live app — appears in live-app-selector). Good.

LiveReviews.jsx exportSheet reads currentApp before calling but there is no visible export-loading toast — a very large CSV would look frozen. Minor UX (button disabled + label change already covers 'Exporting…').

GooglePlaySync trigger prop pattern is clean; live-reviews hero uses a distinct glass-styled button that still shares data-testid='gplay-sync-btn' with Integrations regression pointer. Since Integrations no longer renders the sync button (only a text pointer), the previous duplicate-testid warning from iter_2 is now resolved.
